recipes.title: Ethiopian genfo, light
recipes.summary: A warm Ethiopian breakfast porridge with a firm, smooth texture, a well of fragrant spiced butter and cool Greek yogurt. Less butter and extra yogurt keep this version lighter.

steps.instruction: Measure the wheat flour, water and salt before heating the pan so the porridge can be worked without interruption.
Bring the water and half the salt to a steady boil in a sturdy saucepan.
Add the wheat flour gradually while stirring firmly to prevent dry pockets from forming.
Work the wheat flour mixture against the sides of the pan until it becomes smooth, thick and elastic.
Cover the genfo and cook over low heat until the wheat flour loses its raw taste and the porridge pulls cleanly from the pan.
Melt the butter with the paprika, cumin, ginger and remaining salt until fragrant.
Shape the genfo into a mound and press a deep well into the centre.
Pour the spiced butter into the well and serve the greek yogurt around the genfo.

recipes.storageNotes: Genfo is best eaten immediately while soft and hot. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat with a splash of water. Keep the Greek yogurt separate and add it after reheating.

recipes.title: Ethiopian genfo
recipes.summary: A traditional-style Ethiopian flour porridge worked until smooth and springy, then served with aromatic paprika, cumin and ginger butter and cool Greek yogurt.

steps.instruction: Measure the wheat flour, water and salt before heating the pan so the porridge can be worked continuously.
Bring the water and half the salt to a steady boil in a sturdy saucepan.
Add the wheat flour gradually while stirring firmly to prevent dry pockets from forming.
Work the wheat flour mixture against the sides of the pan until it becomes smooth, thick and elastic.
Cover the genfo and cook over low heat until the wheat flour tastes cooked and the porridge pulls cleanly from the pan.
Melt the butter with the paprika, cumin, ginger and remaining salt until fragrant.
Shape the genfo into a mound and press a deep well into the centre.
Pour the spiced butter into the well and spoon the greek yogurt around the genfo.

recipes.storageNotes: Serve immediately for the best smooth texture. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat with water over low heat. Store the Greek yogurt separately.

recipes.title: Ethiopian genfo, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous Ethiopian breakfast porridge with extra flour, rich spiced butter and plenty of cool Greek yogurt. The firm, warm genfo is especially satisfying on a slow morning.

steps.instruction: Measure the wheat flour, water and salt before heating the pan so the larger batch can be worked without interruption.
Bring the water and half the salt to a steady boil in a sturdy saucepan.
Add the wheat flour gradually while stirring firmly to prevent dry pockets from forming.
Work the wheat flour mixture against the sides of the pan until it becomes smooth, thick and elastic.
Cover the genfo and cook over low heat until the wheat flour is fully cooked and the porridge pulls cleanly from the pan.
Melt the butter with the paprika, cumin, ginger and remaining salt until fragrant.
Shape the genfo into a generous mound and press a deep well into the centre.
Pour the spiced butter into the well and serve the greek yogurt around the genfo.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served hot and freshly made. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat slowly with water, stirring until smooth. Add the refrigerated Greek yogurt only when serving.

recipes.title: Lomo saltado, light
recipes.summary: Peruvian beef sirloin stir-fried with onion, tomatoes, garlic, soy sauce and vinegar, served with roasted potatoes and rice. Extra vegetables keep this version bright and balanced.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 220°C and cut the potato into thick, evenly sized fries.
Coat the potato with half the olive oil and spread the fries across a hot baking tray.
Slice the beef sirloin, onion and tomatoes and chop the garlic and cilantro.
Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender while the potato roasts until golden and crisp at the edges.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a very hot pan and sear the sirloin until browned outside but still juicy.
Add the onion and garlic and stir-fry until the onion is lightly charred but still crisp.
Add the tomatoes, soy sauce and vinegar and toss until the tomatoes soften slightly and the sauce coats the beef.
Fold in the cilantro and serve the lomo saltado with the roasted potato and white rice.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten immediately while the vegetables and potatoes retain their texture. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat the beef gently. Store the rice and potatoes separately.

recipes.title: Lomo saltado
recipes.summary: A classic Peruvian stir-fry of juicy beef sirloin, red-hot onion, tomatoes, soy sauce and vinegar, served with golden potatoes and fluffy rice.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 220°C and cut the potato into thick, evenly sized fries.
Coat the potato with half the olive oil and spread the fries across a hot baking tray.
Slice the beef sirloin, onion and tomatoes and chop the garlic and cilantro.
Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender while the potato roasts until crisp and deeply golden.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a very hot pan and sear the sirloin until browned outside and juicy within.
Add the onion and garlic and stir-fry until the onion has charred edges but remains firm.
Add the tomatoes, soy sauce and vinegar and toss until the sauce becomes glossy.
Fold in the cilantro and serve the lomo saltado with the roasted potato and white rice.

recipes.storageNotes: Serve straight from the pan for the best contrast of textures. Refrigerate for up to 2 days. Reheat the stir-fry quickly over high heat and warm the rice and potatoes separately.

recipes.title: Lomo saltado, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous Peruvian stir-fry with extra beef sirloin, crisp potatoes and rice. Soy sauce, vinegar, tomatoes and charred onion create the dish's familiar savoury, tangy finish.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 220°C and cut the potato into thick, evenly sized fries.
Coat the potato with half the olive oil and spread the fries across two hot baking trays.
Slice the beef sirloin, onion and tomatoes and chop the garlic and cilantro.
Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender while the potato roasts until deeply golden and crisp.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a very hot pan and sear the sirloin in batches until browned and juicy.
Add the onion and garlic and stir-fry until the onion develops charred edges.
Add the tomatoes, soy sauce and vinegar and toss until the sauce coats the sirloin.
Fold in the cilantro and serve the lomo saltado with the roasted potato and white rice.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served immediately. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat the beef quickly to avoid overcooking. Store the rice and potatoes in separate containers.

recipes.title: Polish pork and cabbage stew, light
recipes.summary: A lighter Polish-style cabbage stew with tender pork loin, cured pork, sauerkraut and mushrooms. Extra cabbage keeps the shared pot generous without relying on extra fat.

steps.instruction: Cut the pork loin and cured pork and prepare the cabbage, sauerkraut, mushrooms, onion and garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and brown the loin in batches.
Cook the cured pork in the same pot until its edges begin to colour.
Add the onion and mushrooms and cook until the onion softens and the mushrooms lose their moisture.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, paprika and thyme until the paste darkens slightly.
Add the green cabbage, sauerkraut, beef stock and browned pork loin to the pot.
Cover and simmer the stew gently until the cabbage is tender and the loin is cooked through.
Uncover the pot and simmer until the liquid reduces to a rich coating around the pork and cabbage.
Rest the stew off the heat so the flavours settle.
Stir the Polish pork and cabbage stew before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: The stew improves overnight. Refrigerate for up to 4 days and reheat gently until steaming. Freeze in portions for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Polish pork and cabbage stew
recipes.summary: A deeply savoury Polish-style stew with pork loin, cured pork, sauerkraut, fresh cabbage and mushrooms. Slow simmering blends the smoky, tangy and earthy flavours.

steps.instruction: Cut the pork loin and cured pork and prepare the cabbage, sauerkraut, mushrooms, onion and garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and brown the loin in batches.
Cook the cured pork in the same pot until browned around the edges.
Add the onion and mushrooms and cook until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, paprika and thyme until the paste darkens and smells rich.
Add the green cabbage, sauerkraut, beef stock and browned pork loin to the pot.
Cover and simmer the stew gently until the cabbage is very tender and the loin is succulent.
Uncover the pot and simmer until the cooking liquid becomes thick and savoury.
Rest the stew off the heat so the pork and cabbage absorb the sauce.
Stir the Polish pork and cabbage stew thoroughly before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 4 days; the flavour deepens as it rests. Reheat slowly with a splash of beef stock if needed. Freeze for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Polish pork and cabbage stew, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous Polish-style stew loaded with pork loin, smoky cured pork, sauerkraut, cabbage and mushrooms. Long simmering produces a rich dinner for four hungry diners.

steps.instruction: Cut the pork loin and cured pork and prepare the cabbage, sauerkraut, mushrooms, onion and garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and brown the loin in batches.
Cook the cured pork in the same pot until deeply browned around the edges.
Add the onion and mushrooms and cook until their moisture evaporates and the edges colour.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, paprika and thyme until the paste becomes dark and fragrant.
Add the green cabbage, sauerkraut, beef stock and browned pork loin to the pot.
Cover and simmer the stew gently until the cabbage is meltingly tender and the loin is succulent.
Uncover the pot and simmer until the cooking liquid reduces to a rich sauce.
Rest the stew off the heat so the larger batch settles and absorbs the sauce.
Stir the Polish pork and cabbage stew thoroughly before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps for up to 4 days in the refrigerator and tastes even richer the next day. Reheat gently. Freeze portions for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Chicken cheddar egg muffins, light
recipes.summary: Baked American-style egg muffins with chicken breast, spinach, peppers, spring onions and a little cheddar. They are compact, savoury and naturally high in protein.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C and lightly coat a twelve-hole muffin tin with half the olive oil.
Cook the chicken breast in the remaining olive oil until the breast pieces are opaque and lightly golden.
Dice the bell pepper and slice the spring onions while the chicken cools slightly.
Wilt the spinach in the warm pan until its released moisture has evaporated.
Whisk the eggs with the whole milk and paprika until evenly combined.
Divide the chicken, spinach, bell pepper, spring onions and cheddar cheese between the muffin holes.
Pour the egg mixture into the tin and bake until the muffins are puffed and set in the centre.
Rest the chicken cheddar egg muffins before lifting them from the tin.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and eat cold or reheat briefly until hot. Freeze cooled muffins for up to 2 months and thaw overnight before reheating.

recipes.title: Chicken cheddar egg muffins
recipes.summary: Tender baked egg muffins packed with chicken breast, cheddar, spinach, peppers and spring onions. They make an easy American high-protein snack for meal prep.

Cook the chicken breast in the remaining olive oil until the breast pieces are opaque and lightly golden.
Dice the bell pepper and slice the spring onions while the chicken cools slightly.
Wilt the spinach in the warm pan until its released moisture has evaporated.

Divide the chicken, spinach, bell pepper, spring onions and cheddar cheese between the muffin holes.

recipes.title: Chicken cheddar egg muffins, hearty
recipes.summary: Generous baked egg muffins with extra chicken breast, eggs and cheddar. Spinach, peppers and spring onions keep the substantial high-protein snack colourful and savoury.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C and lightly coat a twelve-hole muffin tin with half the olive oil.
Cook the chicken breast in the remaining olive oil until the breast pieces are golden and cooked through.
Dice the bell pepper and slice the spring onions while the chicken cools slightly.
Wilt the spinach in the warm pan until no visible moisture remains.
Whisk the eggs with the whole milk and paprika until smooth.
Divide the chicken, spinach, bell pepper, spring onions and cheddar cheese between the muffin holes.
Pour the egg mixture into the tin and bake until the large muffins are golden and set in the centre.
Rest the chicken cheddar egg muffins before lifting them carefully from the tin.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat until hot throughout. Freeze cooled muffins individually for up to 2 months for an easy prepared snack.

recipes.title: British breakfast skillet, light
recipes.summary: A lighter British breakfast skillet with eggs, cured pork, mushrooms, spinach and spring onions. The generous vegetables keep it filling while remaining genuinely keto.

steps.instruction: Slice the mushrooms, cured pork and spring onions before heating the skillet.
Melt the butter in a wide frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the cured pork until browned at the edges and hot throughout.
Add the mushrooms and paprika and cook until the mushrooms are golden and their moisture has evaporated.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted but still bright green.
Crack the eggs into the skillet and cook until the whites are set and the yolks remain tender.
Scatter the spring onions over the British breakfast skillet before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten immediately while the eggs are tender. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat gently, though the yolks will become firmer. Do not freeze.

recipes.title: British breakfast skillet
recipes.summary: A hearty British-style breakfast skillet with cured pork, eggs, golden mushrooms, spinach and spring onions. It delivers familiar fry-up flavours without bread, beans or potatoes.

steps.instruction: Slice the mushrooms, cured pork and spring onions before heating the skillet.
Melt the butter in a wide frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the cured pork until deeply browned at the edges and hot throughout.
Add the mushrooms and paprika and cook until the mushrooms are well browned.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted and any released moisture has evaporated.
Crack the eggs into the skillet and cook until the whites are set and the yolks remain tender.
Finish the British breakfast skillet with the spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Serve immediately for the best egg texture. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat over low heat. Freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: British breakfast skillet, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous British keto breakfast with extra cured pork and eggs, plus buttery mushrooms, spinach and spring onions. It is substantial enough for a long morning.

steps.instruction: Slice the mushrooms, cured pork and spring onions before heating the skillet.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the cured pork until crisp at the edges and thoroughly heated.
Add the mushrooms and paprika and cook until deeply golden and dry around the edges.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted and evenly mixed with the pork and mushrooms.
Crack the eggs into the skillet and cook until the whites are set and the yolks reach your preferred consistency.
Scatter the spring onions over the British breakfast skillet and serve hot.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served straight from the skillet. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat gently until hot, accepting that the eggs will become firmer. Do not freeze.
